name: Stereo matching cost-volume architectures: GC-Net (soft-argmin), PSMNet (SPP + stacked hourglass), GwcNet (group-wise correlation), SGM-Net and GA-Net (learned semi-global aggregation), AcfNet (unimodal cost filtering), CFNet (cascade, uncertainty-adaptive range), ACVNet (attention concatenation volume), RAFT-Stereo, IGEV / IGEV++ (geometry encoding volumes, multi-range), CREStereo (cascaded recurrent, adaptive correlation, hard-case synthetic data)
authors_org: GC-Net: Kendall et al. (Skydio/Cambridge). PSMNet: J.-R. Chang, Y.-S. Chen (NCTU). GwcNet: X. Guo et al. (CUHK/SenseTime). SGM-Net: A. Seki, M. Pollefeys (Toshiba/ETH). GA-Net: F. Zhang, V. Prisacariu, R. Yang, P. Torr (Oxford/Baidu). AcfNet: Y. Zhang et al. (DeepMotion). CFNet: Z. Shen, Y. Dai, Z. Rao (NWPU). ACVNet: G. Xu et al. (HUST). RAFT-Stereo: L. Lipson, Z. Teed, J. Deng (Princeton). IGEV / IGEV++: G. Xu, X. Wang, Z. Zhang, J. Cheng, C. Liao, X. Yang (HUST). CREStereo: J. Li et al. (Megvii).
year: 2017 (GC-Net, SGM-Net), 2018 (PSMNet), 2019 (GwcNet, GA-Net), 2020 (AcfNet), 2021 (CFNet, RAFT-Stereo), 2022 (ACVNet, CREStereo), 2023 (IGEV-Stereo), 2025 (IGEV++ in TPAMI)

code_availability: All public: PSMNet github.com/JiaRenChang/PSMNet; GwcNet github.com/xy-guo/GwcNet; GA-Net github.com/feihuzhang/GANet (custom CUDA SGA/LGA kernels); AcfNet in github.com/DeepMotionAIResearch/DenseMatchingBenchmark; CFNet github.com/gallenszl/CFNet; ACVNet github.com/gangweix/ACVNet; RAFT-Stereo github.com/princeton-vl/RAFT-Stereo; IGEV github.com/gangweix/IGEV and IGEV++ github.com/gangweix/IGEV-plusplus; CREStereo github.com/megvii-research/CREStereo (MegEngine; PyTorch ports exist). GC-Net: unofficial re-implementations only [uncertain]. SGM-Net: no official code [uncertain].
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed (ICCV/CVPR/AAAI/3DV/TPAMI) with public benchmarks; IGEV++ and CREStereo abstracts verified this session; other details from the papers as widely documented. Transfer to our 1-D-lateral x level setting is our own reasoning, not evidence.
extreme_summary: Deep stereo builds a cost volume (per pixel, per candidate disparity), aggregates it with 3D convolutions or learned SGM-like recurrences, and reads out disparity by soft-argmin, with later work adding learned matching features, group-wise correlation, multi-range volumes and iterative GRU refinement. Our model already is a GC-Net-style design collapsed by one dimension (MD x level cost image, 2D U-Net aggregation, softmax expectation). The untried pieces that map most directly onto our error anatomy are learned semi-global aggregation along MD (GA-Net SGA), learned matching features/group-wise correlation instead of a single handcrafted |gr - tw_gr| cost, PSMNet-style intermediate supervision, and CREStereo-style hard-case synthetic data; RAFT/IGEV-style iterative refinement is the family that already failed here.
task_definition: Stereo: predict per-pixel disparity d(x, y) of a rectified image pair, i.e. for each left-image pixel choose which of D candidate right-image positions matches. Ours (analogy documented in kaggle_1st_place/CLAUDE.md): for each MD column of the lateral, choose which of 400 typewell levels (0.25 ft over a 100 ft window) the lateral is at, i.e. TVT is disparity, the typewell is the right image scanline, and the lateral GR is the left image.
inputs: Stereo: two RGB images; features from a shared (Siamese) CNN. Ours: 16-channel image of 345 MD columns x 400 levels built by hand: tw_gr, gr, gr_abs_diff (a single-scale absolute-difference cost), per-column lateral window statistics (gr_std, gr_slope, quadratic fit, first-last delta, isnan rate), tw_gr_is_nan, tw_tvt_rel, seen_tvt_rel, tw_seen_tvt_abs_diff, z_diff (optionally PF channels).
target_parameterisation: Stereo: disparity (continuous), regressed via expectation over discrete candidates; cascade methods (CFNet, CREStereo) re-parameterise as residual disparity within a narrowed range. Ours: TVT - TVT0 over the fixed 400-level window, supervised by regression plus an 'alignment' density target (exp_smooth, sigma 1.25 levels).
output_representation: Per-pixel softmax over disparity (GC-Net, PSMNet, GwcNet, GA-Net, AcfNet, CFNet stages, ACVNet) or per-pixel scalar disparity updated iteratively (RAFT-Stereo, IGEV, CREStereo). AcfNet additionally predicts a per-pixel confidence (variance) of the target distribution. Ours: per-column softmax over 400 levels, expectation decode.
architecture: GC-Net: Siamese 2D CNN features at 1/2 res -> concatenation cost volume (C x D/2 x H/2 x W/2) -> 3D conv encoder-decoder -> soft-argmin. PSMNet: ResNet features + spatial pyramid pooling (global context) -> concatenation volume at 1/4 res -> three stacked 3D hourglasses with intermediate outputs, each supervised (weights 0.5/0.7/1.0) -> upsample + soft-argmin. GwcNet: split feature channels into G groups, correlation per group gives a G-channel volume (plus a reduced concatenation volume) -> cheaper and better-conditioned aggregation. SGM-Net: CNN predicts the SGM P1/P2 penalties per pixel/direction, classic SGM does the aggregation. GA-Net: semi-global guided aggregation (SGA) layer: for each direction r, C_A(p,d) = w0*C(p,d) + w1*C_A(p-r,d) + w2*C_A(p-r,d-1) + w3*C_A(p-r,d+1) + w4*max_i C_A(p-r,i), weights predicted per pixel by a guidance subnet and normalised, max over 4 directions; plus local guided aggregation (LGA) for thin structures; a few GA layers replace most 3D convs at far lower cost. AcfNet: standard PSMNet-like pipeline, but supervises the cost volume with a per-pixel unimodal (Laplacian) distribution centred on ground truth with learned variance from a confidence head. CFNet: fused multi-scale volumes at low res, then cascade stages whose disparity search range is set per pixel from the previous stage's variance (mean +- k*sigma). ACVNet: correlation volume used to build attention weights that filter the concatenation volume, suppressing redundant/ambiguous matches before aggregation. RAFT-Stereo: all-pairs 1-D correlation pyramid (no 3D conv), multi-level ConvGRU updates the disparity iteratively (sequence loss). IGEV: a lightweight 3D-regularised geometry encoding volume (GEV) + all-pairs correlation; soft-argmin from the GEV initialises the ConvGRU updates, cutting iterations. IGEV++: multi-range GEVs (coarse volumes for large disparities / ill-posed regions, fine ones for detail), adaptive patch matching (APM) to build large-range costs cheaply, selective geometry feature fusion (SGFF) to combine ranges per pixel. CREStereo: cascaded recurrent refinement over a feature pyramid, adaptive group correlation layer (local 2D-1D alternating search with learned deformable offsets and group-wise correlation), stacked cascade at inference for high resolution, trained on a new synthetic dataset built around hard cases.
core_mechanism: Three recurring ideas. (1) Matching is done in a learned feature space with receptive field, not on raw intensities, and the cost is expressed as correlation/concatenation of Siamese features (GC-Net, GwcNet, ACVNet). (2) Ambiguity (repeated texture, textureless or occluded regions) is resolved by propagating evidence across the image under a smoothness prior: 3D conv hourglasses with global context (PSMNet SPP), or explicitly DP-like learned aggregation with a jump penalty and an 'any disparity' reset term (SGM-Net, GA-Net). (3) Coarse-to-fine: a coarse global volume handles large displacements and ambiguous regions, fine volumes or iterative updates handle detail (CFNet, IGEV++, CREStereo, RAFT-Stereo). AcfNet adds a fourth: regularising the shape of the predicted distribution so soft-argmin is not a blend of modes.
training_objective: Smooth-L1 on soft-argmin disparity (GC-Net, PSMNet with multi-output weights, GwcNet, GA-Net); AcfNet adds stereo focal loss / cross-entropy to a unimodal target with learned variance plus confidence loss; CFNet multi-stage smooth-L1; RAFT-Stereo, IGEV, CREStereo exponentially weighted sequence loss over refinement iterations. Ours: regression (0.05/3) + alignment density (0.2/3, exp_smooth sigma 1.25) + GR_penalty (0.05/3); deep supervision implemented in the decoder but off (deep_sup=False).
decoding: Soft-argmin / expectation over disparity (GC-Net family); iterative scalar updates (RAFT family); some works use top-k or local soft-argmin around the argmax to avoid mode blending (covered in B03).
metric_consistent_decode: Soft-argmin = posterior mean, Bayes-optimal for squared error given a calibrated posterior, which matches our pooled RMSE; stereo's benchmarks (bad-pixel %, EPE) reward mode-seeking, so stereo papers that replace soft-argmin with argmax-local decodes optimise a different metric and may raise our RMSE. Cascade range narrowing (CFNet/IGEV++ fine stages, CREStereo) is implicitly mode-seeking when the posterior is multimodal.
evidence_scope: Whole image pair (global context via SPP, hourglasses, or directional recurrences spanning the full width). For us the equivalent is the whole lateral suffix plus prefix in one pass, which our U-Net already sees (bottleneck 22 MD x 13 levels).
prefix_conditioning: Not applicable in stereo. In ours the known prefix enters as channels (seen_tvt_rel, tw_seen_tvt_abs_diff); a GA-Net-style directional aggregation run from heel to toe would naturally propagate the known prefix's band identity along MD.
propose_vs_select: Single output per pixel; CFNet/IGEV++ can be read as propose (coarse range) then select (fine), and multi-range volumes could provide band hypotheses to a reranker. Stereo nets are ensemble-compatible only as additional members with shared inputs.
physical_constraints: Smoothness with discontinuity tolerance (SGM penalties P1 for +-1 disparity, P2 for jumps; GA-Net's learned w2/w3 and w4 terms); uniqueness/occlusion handling is not modelled in most. Maps to ours as: TVT changes slowly along MD (small |dTVT/dMD| per column), with rare faults (jumps).
dataset: SceneFlow (~35k synthetic pairs), KITTI 2012/2015 (~400 real driving pairs), Middlebury, ETH3D; CREStereo adds ~200k-pair synthetic set designed for hard cases [uncertain on exact count]; IGEV++ evaluated up to 768 px disparities on SceneFlow. Our analogue: 773 real Kaggle laterals (618 train) + 85% synthetic wells from Ruby's simulator.
synthetic_to_real: Standard stereo recipe is heavy synthetic pretraining (SceneFlow) then small real fine-tuning; CREStereo shows that designing synthetic data around the hard cases (repetitive texture, textureless, thin structures, lighting) is what improves real-world ambiguity handling. Our training is already ~85% synthetic with no separate real-only fine-tuning stage [uncertain whether a real-only finetune has been tried].
metric_and_performance: IGEV++: 3.23% bad-2.0 on Middlebury large-disparity/ill-posed regions, 31.9% and 54.8% better than RAFT-Stereo and GMStereo there; best across disparity ranges up to 768 px on SceneFlow. GA-Net: SGA/LGA layers matched or beat many 3D conv layers at a fraction of compute on SceneFlow/KITTI, with visible gains in occluded and large textureless/reflective regions [uncertain on exact numbers]. PSMNet: first on KITTI 2015 at publication (D1-all ~2.32%). CREStereo: 1st on Middlebury and ETH3D at submission. AcfNet: improved over PSMNet on SceneFlow/KITTI at publication. Ours: AcfNet-style unimodal target +0.162 ft (worse), RAFT-style 8-iteration refinement +0.078 ft (worse, unstable after epoch 40), MD-axial attention -0.024 ft (not distinguishable from the -0.030 seed null), all at 60 epochs vs a 5.1618 baseline.
comparability: Not comparable numerically (image benchmarks, bad-pixel/EPE metrics). Architectural comparability is high: our 2D cost image is GC-Net's 3D volume with the image-height axis removed, so 3D-aggregation ideas transfer as 2D ops and 2D-recurrence ideas (SGA along image rows) transfer as 1D recurrences along MD.
validation_protocol: Stereo: fixed public benchmarks with hidden test sets. For our repo: 155-well holdout, single-run noise +-0.39 ft, seed-level null -0.03 ft at 60 epochs; 60-epoch comparisons are confounded by undertraining (baseline 5.16 -> 4.98 at 150), so architecture candidates need 150 epochs and 2 seeds.
inference_budget: SGA-style aggregation over 173 x 100 (1/2 MD, 1/4 level) with ~32 channels, 2 directions: sequential over 173 steps but tiny tensors; a few ms per well on GPU, tens of ms on CPU [uncertain until measured]. Group-wise correlation channels: negligible. Stacked hourglass/intermediate supervision: training-only cost if the extra heads are dropped at inference. Iterative RAFT/IGEV refinement: +8-32 update passes, the most expensive and already failed.
repeated_layers: In stereo, repeated texture is the canonical ambiguity. Remedies with evidence: (a) wider context from SPP/hourglasses (PSMNet), which our U-Net already has; (b) learned semi-global aggregation (SGM-Net, GA-Net) that carries a match hypothesis along a scanline with learned continuity and jump penalties, so a locally ambiguous region inherits the band chosen where evidence is unambiguous; (c) attention filtering of the volume using correlation confidence (ACVNet); (d) hard-case synthetic training data (CREStereo). For us, (b) is the in-network, end-to-end trained version of the post-hoc forward-backward continuity decode that failed; unlike the post-hoc decode it can learn when to trust continuity and its outputs are trained against the RMSE-consistent loss. Caveat: our posterior dump shows much of the error is choosing/blending between bands that are all locally consistent over long MD stretches, and continuity cannot break a tie that persists along the whole lateral.
drift: Coarse/multi-range volumes (IGEV++, CFNet) target large displacements, relevant if part of the drift error comes from truth leaving the +-50 ft window or sitting near its edge (clipping); fine-resolution detail is lost in our stem (level axis stride 4 at the stem, 400 -> 100), analogous to building the volume at 1/4 resolution. A slow one-line drift is a smooth bias, not an ambiguity, so matching architectures help only if the evidence to correct it (fine GR texture alignment) is being discarded early.
uncertainty_and_calibration: AcfNet's confidence head and CFNet's variance-based ranges are the stereo uncertainty mechanisms; neither is calibrated in the ECE sense. For our RMSE, calibration of band weights is what matters (B09); none of these architectures addresses it directly.
where_to_use: (1) Aggregation: insert GA-Net-style SGA layers along MD (heel-to-toe and toe-to-heel) into the decoder at the 1/2-MD, 1/4-level scale (173 x 100) or the next scale (87 x 50), zero-gated residual, guidance weights predicted from decoder features. (2) Cost construction: add learned matching-feature channels before the U-Net: a 1-D CNN over typewell GR along the level axis (full 0.25 ft resolution) and a 1-D CNN over the raw 32 lateral rows of each column (GR vs relative z within the column), combined by group-wise correlation (GwcNet) into G extra channels, replacing or supplementing the single handcrafted gr_abs_diff. (3) Supervision: turn on the already-implemented deep_sup (PSMNet-style intermediate outputs). (4) Range: diagnose whether truth ever leaves the 100 ft window; if yes, an IGEV++-style coarse long-range volume (e.g. 300 ft at 1 ft) as extra channels or branch. (5) Data: CREStereo's hard-case synthetic design (see A19/B11).
error_mode_targeted: Band confusion (~51%) via SGA propagation and learned matching features; broad/skewed humps (~13%) via finer-resolution learned costs; drift (~25%) only via the range/resolution diagnostics.
gap_vs_our_implementation: What we already have: cost image + 2D encoder-decoder aggregation + softmax expectation (GC-Net/PSMNet skeleton); global context through a ConvNeXt-small U-Net; concatenation-volume-like inputs (tw_gr broadcast along MD and gr broadcast along levels). What we tried and failed at 60 epochs: AcfNet unimodal target (replacing alignment, +0.162), RAFT refinement (+0.078, unstable), MD-axial attention (-0.024, gates barely opened), large-kernel convs (never trained due to a zero-init deadlock; still untested). What we do not do: (a) no learned matching features; the only cost is pointwise |gr - tw_gr| at a single scale (the +-0.25 ft shifted variants tw_gr_m0p25/p0p25 and signed/min/max diffs exist but are commented out), and the lateral descriptors are handcrafted window statistics; (b) no DP-like learned aggregation along MD (SGM-Net/GA-Net): long-range propagation relies on the U-Net's downsampled bottleneck and failed post-hoc DP; (c) no intermediate supervision (deep_sup implemented but False); (d) level axis is downsampled 4x at the stem, so aggregation never runs at 0.25 ft level resolution, unlike stereo nets that keep 1/4 but build the cost from learned features; (e) fixed single 100 ft range with no coarse long-range volume; (f) no hard-case synthetic design.
proposed_experiment: E0 (CPU diagnostics, no training): from results/baseline_check_posterior_all compute (i) fraction of holdout rows whose true TVT - TVT0 lies outside or within 2 ft of the +-50 ft window edge and their share of squared error (decides the multi-range lead); (ii) for wrong_mode columns, the MD run length over which the wrong band stays locally consistent with GR (if wrong bands persist over most of the lateral, SGA cannot help; if they are islands between confidently-correct stretches, SGA can). E1 (SGA along MD, main candidate): new module SGAlongMD in experiments/arch/seq_NN_arch_blocks.py: input decoder feature map F (B,C,H=MD,W=level), a 1x1 conv to K=16 'cost' channels, a guidance head predicting 5 weights per (MD, channel group) normalised by softmax, recurrence over MD in both directions (torch loop over H, or cumulative formulation), output = F + gamma * conv1x1(max(fwd, bwd)), gamma initialised to 0 with the inner convs at normal init (avoid the arch_v4 zero-times-zero deadlock). Register in model_modules() and model_named_parameters() (trap documented in CLAUDE.md). Place at decoder scale 173 x 100. cfg arch_v5_sga; 150 epochs, 2 seeds, vs 0801_V2_ep150 plus a second baseline seed; accept only if both seeds improve and the mean gain exceeds the seed scatter; log gamma to confirm it opened. E2 (learned cost): channels from a Siamese-style pair of small 1-D CNNs (typewell along levels at 0.25 ft; lateral per column over its 32 raw rows with relative z), group-wise correlation G=8 -> +8 input channels; trained end-to-end (cfg arch_v6_gwc); same protocol. E3 (cheap): flip deep_sup=True with deep_sup_stage_decay 0.5 on the baseline, 150 epochs 2 seeds. E4 (only if E0(i) shows window-edge error): coarse 300 ft x 1 ft range channels resampled onto the 400-level grid or a parallel coarse branch.
implementation_effort: E0 low (numpy on existing dumps). E1 medium (~150 lines; a Python loop over 173 MD steps is simple but slow in training, a scan/cumulative-max CUDA-friendly form or torch.compile helps; must respect gating/registration traps). E2 medium (dataset must expose raw 32-row lateral windows per column to the model, currently only summary stats are passed). E3 trivial (config flag). E4 medium.
gpu_cost: E1: SGA over 173 x 100 x 16 channels x 2 directions adds maybe 10-30% to the ~110-120 s/epoch ConvNeXt-small baseline on the RTX 5060 8 GB [uncertain until measured]; 150 epochs ~5-6 h per run, 4 runs (2 seeds x candidate/control, control shared) ~ 12-24 h. E2: small 1-D CNNs, negligible compute, memory +8 channels. E3: training-only extra heads, negligible.
distillation_compatibility: KD on output posteriors works regardless of teacher architecture. For the FastViT student, SGA can be added to the student's decoder too (cheap, but a sequential op on CPU) or left teacher-only so the student learns the propagated posterior. Learned cost channels (E2) must be computed for the student as well; they are small 1-D CNNs and fit the CPU budget.
error_correlation_with_ours: Moderate-to-high correlation: same inputs and decode. SGA changes the inductive bias (explicit continuity along MD) and may produce different errors on wells where the U-Net blends bands, so an SGA model may be a useful member of the existing ConvNeXt average; learned per-point gates have failed before, so plain averaging is preferred.
risk: (1) Our model already sees the whole lateral in one pass and the posterior-analysis summary says band-confusion error falls only with more evidence or better calibration; SGA and learned costs add no new evidence, only better use of existing evidence, so gains may be small relative to the +-0.39 ft single-run noise. (2) Post-hoc continuity decoding already failed, suggesting wrong bands are often continuous along MD, which no continuity prior can fix (E0(ii) tests this). (3) Recurrent/iterative modules were unstable here (RAFT peaked at epoch 40) and residual branches grafted onto the pretrained ConvNeXt barely opened in 60 epochs (axial gates ~0.01); 150 epochs and a verified-live gate are required. (4) Mode-seeking parts of stereo (cascade range narrowing, argmax-local decodes, unimodal targets) conflict with the RMSE-optimal expectation decode; AcfNet-style unimodality already hurt (+0.162). (5) Benchmarks are images with bad-pixel metrics; no evidence that stereo gains transfer to 1-D well-log alignment. (6) Holdout resolution: the pooled metric is decided by ~10 wells, so E1-E3 need seeds or 5-fold CV to conclude.
notes: Mapping table (ours -> stereo): MD column = image column; TVT level = disparity; typewell GR = right scanline; lateral GR = left scanline; gr_abs_diff = AD cost volume (SAD without window); ConvNeXt U-Net = 3D cost aggregation (2D here because the image height axis does not exist); softmax expectation = GC-Net soft-argmin; alignment loss = AcfNet-like fixed-width target; PF channels = external prior as in DEFOM-Stereo/MonSter (B02). A key difference from stereo: laterals revisit TVT non-monotonically and there is no epipolar uniqueness, so occlusion reasoning does not transfer. The survey by Tosi et al. (2024) is the best entry point for newer variants (Selective-Stereo CVPR 2024 with multi-frequency GRUs; Stereo Anywhere; foundation-prior models in B02). Multimodal decoding and losses (ADL, SMD-Nets, top-k soft-argmax) are split into B03; learned DP losses into B05. Overlaps: A19 (CREStereo hard-case synthetic data), B02, B03, B05.
